newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia upbeat as H1 digital handsets soar.
newsitem.headline: Nokia upbeat as H1 digital handsets soar.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said on Monday sales of digital mobile phones rose 94 percent in the first half of the year, and that the first half performance overall supported its previous positive outlook.

"The results meet our performance targets and give us reason to maintain our previously stated positive outlook for strong growth and good profitability for the whole year," it said in a statement with its first half results.
"Sales of our digital handsets grew by 94 percent in the first half of 1997 compared to the same period a year ago, solidifying our leading market position," it said.

"We believe that our CDMA phone, with deliveries now starting in the U.S., will continue to enhance our leadership in digital mobile phones," Nokia said, adding it would also invest in exisiting analog systems which show market opportunities.
Nokia reported first half pretax profit at 3.33 billion markka -- 1.88 billion markka in the second quarter -- compared to 1.13 billion in the year-ago period, and exceeding forecasts.

The mean forecast had been for a 3.09 billion markka first half profit, or 1.64 billion in the second quarter, and the highest forecast had been 3.30 billion in January-June or 1.85 billion in the second quarter.
Nokia also said it was very satisfied with growth in infrastructure order inflow, "which clearly surpassed market growth".
